newsitem.title: USA: Most workers now insured through managed care:study.
newsitem.headline: Most workers now insured through managed care:study.

text.p: Almost three out of every four workers who get health insurance on the job are now covered by managed care, including health maintenance organizations (HMOs), a new study said Sunday.

That is a 50 percent increase in just two years, according to Gail Jensen, a professor at Detroit's Wayne State University, whose findings appear in the January-February edition of the journal Health Affairs.
Jensen and her colleagues collaborated with KPMG Peat Marwick in conducting two surveys of employers and workers tracking trends from 1993-95.

Numerous studies have found that fewer and fewer people are getting insurance on the job. Working people with no insurance and their dependents constitute a large share of the roughly 40 million uninsured Americans.
But for those who still get group insurance at work, managed care is now the most common option.
"Managed care isn't coming, it has arrived," Jensen and her colleagues wrote.
All forms of managed care rose, but the more flexible arrangements that give participants greater choice grew especially fast.

Among managed care enrollees, participation in "point-of-service" options that let a patient see a doctor outside the plan for only a modest additional payment has doubled from 9 percent in 1993 to 20 percent in 1995.
